text:
Sam Steel hasn't recorded a point in twelve straight games, an odd thing to be true while the Stars keep winning around him. He's still playing almost 16 minutes a night in a checking role that includes the penalty kill, and Dallas keeps giving him the job. The scoresheet just hasn't noticed: 3 points in 20 games.

How much of it is him? Some of each. He has 1 goal on 3.2 expected (the quality of his chances), and the Stars have scored 5.9 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, a gap that usually closes. But the chances have thinned out during the drought too, and Dallas is taking 47% of the expected goals with him out there at five on five. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found last season that 55% of his shots came off the rush, so his best moments come right after a turnover. Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.1 wins above replacement in 2025-26, a useful depth player. Our numbers project about 27 points. Watch whether his line starts finding those rush chances again.
headline: Sam Steel's drought amid a Dallas winning run
